processing: Used for Yibin early tea, which is spread to cool, fixed, straightened and shaped, dried and sorted, with no oxidation.
harvest_season: Very early spring. In Jiang'an County it comes in after Emei Wenchun and Wuniuzao, alongside Fuding Dabai, within a picking run that lasts from January to March.
appearance_dry: As Yibin early tea: flat, straight, neat buds with a glossy bright green colour.
appearance_liquor: Tender green and bright, as is usual for Yibin early tea.
appearance_wet: Tender, bright green buds, as is usual for Yibin early tea.
taste_profile: Yibin early tea generally has a chestnut-like aroma and a fresh, mellow sweetness; no tasting note specific to this cultivar is well established.

brewing.notes: A glass suits flat bud tea. Keep the water cool or the fresh edge goes bitter quickly.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name; it usually goes into Yibin early tea, sold as the current year's very early spring picking. The earliest lots carry the premium, and like other greens it is best drunk within the year.
description:
Fuxuan No. 9 is a tea cultivar grown in Yibin, in southern Sichuan, where it is one of the main plants behind Yibin early tea. Yibin's selling point is simply how soon its gardens wake up, and this cultivar is part of the relay that keeps fresh buds coming.

Growers in Jiang'an County stagger their cultivars: Emei Wenchun goes first, then Wuniuzao, then Fuxuan No. 9 and Fuding Dabai. The leaf then follows the Yibin early tea routine of cooling, fixing, shaping and drying, which gives a flat, straight bud.

In a study comparing Yibin early tea made from three cultivars, Mingshan 131 led on liquor colour and aroma and Wuniuzao on taste, so Fuxuan No. 9 is not the standout of that group. Expect the class character rather than a loud signature: chestnut aroma and a fresh, mellow cup. Use cool water and a short first steep.

You will mostly buy it as Yibin early tea, so ask the seller for the picking date and, if you care, the cultivar. Comparing it with a Wuniuzao from the same garden is an easy way to learn what cultivar does.
history: Where and when Fuxuan No. 9 was bred is little documented in openly available material. What is on record is its working life in Yibin, where it is named among the main cultivars for Yibin early tea, and a 2024 article in Chaye Tongxun used it as one of three test cultivars for that tea.
